title: Soil Organic Carbon Enhancement in Intensive Cereal-Pulse Rotations
excerpt: Practical protocols for boosting active soil microbial biomass and humic fractions without disrupting seasonal cropping cycles.
content: Intensive cropping without organic replenishment depletes soil organic carbon (SOC) below the threshold level of 0.5%, impairing aggregate stability and nutrient buffer capacity. By adopting summer green manuring with Sesbania (Dhaincha) or Sunn hemp, incorporating paddy/wheat straw with cellulolytic fungal inoculants, and applying well-aerated compost @ 5 tonnes/ha, farmers can increase organic carbon by 0.15% over a 3-year cycle.
author: Dr. Virendra Singh Tomar

title: Bio-Priming & Seed Inoculation: The First Shield Against Seedling Blight
excerpt: A step-by-step field guide to simultaneous Rhizobium and Trichoderma inoculation on pulses and oilseeds.
content: Bio-priming integrates controlled seed hydration with biological antagonist inoculation. For chickpea and soybean, treating seeds with Trichoderma viride WP @ 5g/kg seed followed by dual liquid Rhizobium + PSB @ 10ml/kg seed enhances germination vigour by 14% and creates an active fungal rhizosphere mantle preventing seedling wilt even in damp black soils.
author: Dr. Anandita Sengupta
institution: ICAR - Indian Institute of Soybean Research

title: Direct Seeding of Rice (DSR) & Laser Levelling: Water-Smart Agriculture
excerpt: How precision land grading combined with pneumatic seed drill implements reduces irrigation water needs by 30%.
content: Laser land levelling levels fields within ±2 cm tolerance, eliminating high and low water stagnation spots. When followed by calibrated tractor-mounted multi-crop drills for Direct Seeded Rice (DSR) or wheat, diesel consumption drops by 20%, weed infestation decreases by 40%, and water footprint is drastically reduced compared to conventional puddle transplanting.
author: Er. Sukhwinder Dhillon

title: Ration Balancing & Silage Preparation for High-Yielding Dairy Bovines
excerpt: Optimizing roughage-to-concentrate ratios and packing bunker silage to sustain peak milk production through dry winter months.
content: Feeding high-producing Murrah and Gir cattle with unbalanced grain concentrates causes sub-acute ruminal acidosis (SARA). Feeding green maize/sorghum silage harvested at the 50% milk-dough stage, combined with bypass fat (100g/day) and chelated mineral mixtures, maintains rumen pH at 6.4-6.8 and elevates milk fat test by 0.4 to 0.6 percentage points.
author: Dr. Hemant Bhargava

title: Ecological Management of Fall Armyworm and Pod Borer in Rabi Pulses
excerpt: Utilizing pheromone traps, bird perches, and Beauveria bassiana sprays before resorting to chemical insecticides.
content: Integrated Pest Management in gram relies on proactive threshold monitoring. Installing 5 funnel pheromone traps per acre provides early alert for Helicoverpa armigera moth flights. Erecting T-shaped wooden bird perches (15/acre) encourages insectivorous birds. If larval counts exceed 1 caterpillar per meter row, applying Beauveria bassiana 1.15% WP @ 1.2 kg/acre provides 82% control without harming predatory ladybird beetles.
author: Dr. Manpreet Kaur Gill
